<thought>The mass spectrum shows a classic carbon isotopic envelope: a dominant monoisotopic peak followed by a series of peaks at +1, +2, +3 … Da with intensities decreasing roughly in a binomial fashion (≈20 % at +1, ≈2 % at +2, ≈0.1 % at +3, etc.). This pattern is uniquely diagnostic of the presence of carbon atoms in the molecule. No other common element produces such a multi‑peak envelope; elements like Cl, Br give only two peaks, and isotopes of H, N, O, S are too low in abundance to generate the observed series. Therefore, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
